characterization_methods.key_findings: Composition of the polycrystalline Fe-9%Al alloy determined as 9.1 at.% (4.6 wt.-%) Al; impurities C 60 wt.ppm and Si 80 wt.ppm (Table 1).
Coarse grain structure with grain sizes of the order of 1 mm; as-cast alloys contained no second phases.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: specimens etched by an alcoholic 10% nitric acid solution

analytical_models.equation_role: describes the linear increase of yield stress with solute (Al) content
analytical_models.model_name: Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys
analytical_models.model_note: The present ~2.2 GPa coefficient for polycrystalline alloys contrasts with the ~1 GPa reported for monocrystals; attributed to differences in alloy preparation (as-cast polycrystals vs. annealed monocrystals) and slip mode (multiple slip vs. single slip).

parameters.name: yield-stress increase per unit% Al, 10^-2 s^-1
yield-stress increase per unit% Al, 10^-4 s^-1

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys fits the experimentally observed linear increase of the room-temperature yield stress with Al content up to 18 at.% for the polycrystalline as-cast alloys.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Binary Fe-Al alloys prepared by vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles using Fe with 99.99% purity (purified by zone melting to minimise impurity content) and Al with 99.999% purity.
Solidified in Cu moulds to obtain rods usually with 18 mm diameter; the alloys were used as-cast, i.e. without any subsequent heat treatment (the as-cast baseline state).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Yield stress = 0.2% proof stress in compression with total straining of at least 5%; results averaged over 2 (yield) or 3-4 (tension) specimens differing by 3% at most
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression specimens 5 × 5 × 10 mm^3; cylindrical tensile specimens per DIN 50125
measurement_conditions.strain_rate: 10^-4 s^-1 and 10^-2 s^-1 (compression); 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^-2 s^-1 (tension)

elongation.value: elongation before necking and fracture strain both decrease with increasing Al content

ultimate_tensile_strength.value: parallels the yield stress (increases linearly with Al content); about 80 MPa higher at -100 °C than at room temperature

yield_stress.direction: polycrystalline as-cast series, 0-18 at.% Al (includes Fe-9%Al); composition dependence
yield_stress.value: linear increase of 21 MPa per unit% Al at 10^-2 s^-1 and 23 MPa per unit% Al at 10^-4 s^-1

structures.overall_structure: Coarse-grained, single-phase (disordered bcc Fe-Al solid solution) polycrystalline microstructure; the as-cast condition contains no second phases. Fe-9 at.% Al lies below the ~10 at.% Al threshold for the onset of ordering reactions.

unmapped_findings: The Fe-9%Al as-cast alloy is one of the polycrystalline alloys listed in Table 1 (nominal 9 at.% Al; real 9.1 at.% / 4.6 wt.-% Al; impurities C 60 wt.ppm, Si 80 wt.ppm). Its Al content is below the ~10 at.% Al threshold for ordering, so it is a disordered bcc solid solution.

Room-temperature compressive yield stress of the polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys increases linearly with Al content up to 18 at.% Al, corresponding to Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys; the hardening coefficient is about 2.2 GPa (i.e. 21 MPa per unit% Al at 10^-2 s^-1 and 23 MPa per unit% Al at 10^-4 s^-1), insensitive to deformation rate and temperature. This trend is the value relevant to the Fe-9%Al as-cast sample, though no individual numeric yield stress is printed for the 9% alloy in Fig. 3.
For the polycrystalline as-cast alloys the tensile yield stress equals the compressive yield stress at the same rate and temperature; the ultimate tensile strength parallels the yield stress.
At -100 °C the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength of the polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys are higher than at room temperature by about 80 MPa.

Ductility (strain before necking and fracture strain) of the polycrystalline as-cast alloys decreases with increasing Al content; ductile fracture with necking occurs up to about 15 at.% Al at room temperature and to about 12 at.% Al at -100 °C, with a transition to brittle fracture without necking in the range 15-18 at.% Al (RT) and 12-14 at.% Al (-100 °C).

Deformation twinning (indicated by large load drops and audible clicks) occurred at room temperature only for the Fe-18%Al alloy, whereas at -100 °C it occurred for Al contents in the range 11-18%; the number of sufficiently mobile dislocations decreases with increasing Al content and decreasing temperature.

The as-cast polycrystalline alloys contained no second phases; fine thin platelike or rod-like (carbide) precipitates appear on grain boundaries only after slow furnace cooling from 1100 °C or prolonged heat treatments (e.g. 14 days at 320 °C), so none are expected in this as-cast Fe-9%Al sample.

Yield-stress drops and stress-strain serrations observed at -100 °C for low-Al as-cast alloys (Fe-4%Al and Fe-6%Al) are attributed to the interaction of mobile dislocations with excess (quenched-in) vacancies.

Short-range ordering in the studied alloys (formed at temperatures below 600 °C, most strongly in the 13-18 at.% Al range) has no major impact on the deformation behaviour; only heat treatments above 600 °C affect the mechanical behaviour of Fe-Al alloys significantly.
